answer: Reputation mirror curve. Each new identity starts with a capacity score set by the median score of its referrers, so isolated clusters inherit a low ceiling that decays geometrically with cluster depth—like a karst sinkhole, each layer narrows the reachable market. An attacker must acquire and sustain diverse, high-score histories per identity, paying the full renewal cost of each fake history every epoch. Cost per identity grows roughly exponentially with cluster size, turning mass registration into a nebula of cheap nodes that cannot transact at scale.
